page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.l: ad conventum, primùm detrimento id non
esset appellanti, deinde præter emansitationis
pœnam usitatam, quinque etiam marcas
fisco solveret: si latam ab eo sententiam con-
firmari contingeret, potestatem haberet to-
tam causam porrò definiendi, etiamsi anno
suo evoluto magistratu jam abiisset: ad con-
ventum judicialem coeuntibus judicandi
gratiâ quantumvis raro numero jus esset ac
potestas causas definiendi, non secus ac si
frequentes convenissent: Conventus hujus-
modi Groningæ agerentur quotannis quater
aut sæpius, si Reip. ratio id videretur po-
scere: esset-que in eo, ut & in tempore con-
ventuum designando, arbitrium prætorum
ab oppidanis datorum (Hovetmannos vo-
cant) & eorum qui res per [?]Agrum in tri-
bunalibus inferioribus judicant: Deinde de
fontium pœnis aut mulctis hæc: Furti,

l.i: receptare fas non esset, aut pœnis eripere:

main_text.l: pœna omnium horum, supplicium capitis.
Cædes cujusvis hominis in conventu publico
præsentis, aut ìstuc euntis, aut redeuntis
ab eo, mulctâ lueretur sexcuplâ: idem juris
de vulnere, aliâve injuriâ esset: Consulis

page.notes: Printed text runs in mixed roman and italic; italic passages are marked. "per Agrum" has a symbol before "Agrum" that I could not read with confidence. The line "ratio id videretur poscere" is hyphenated as "po-scere" at the line end. The printed "esset-que" is shown with the printed word break "esset-que" kept as one word. The final word "Consulis" ends the page and the catchword "verò" is at the foot. The printed "aut ìstuc" has a stray accent mark over "i", which I have left as printed.
